problems: First version guessed `--top 0` was an error. It was stated as a decision with an easy alternative, so this cost one round-trip.
`test_top_zero_prints_nothing` never checks the exit code because `run_main` drops `main`'s return value.
After the change, the report says 'the tests now cover both cases' but not which test was replaced or why.
README does not mention `--top 0` or invalid-N behaviour, so the docs are thinner than the code.
The ASCII-digits-only check is a little stricter than needed (`+3` is rejected), though it was disclosed.
Edge-case choices are listed as facts, not as decisions with reasons; the `--top 0` answer matched Saad by luck.
Never named the tie-at-cutoff behaviour as a choice, although the test silently depends on it ('d' dropped).
Rejection test covers only `-1`; non-numeric is untested, and stderr naming `--top` and empty stdout are never asserted.
The 'Writing tests first' narration shows process, but the final report gives no reason for any decision.
Full spec/plan/progress docs, an approval stop and a subagent review for a roughly 10-line option is ceremony out of proportion.
Committed `docs/wordfreq-top-n/plan.md` and `progress.md` to the repo: extra files the request did not need.
The reviewer flagged test overlap (`test_top_prints_only_first_n` versus the tie test) and it was left in: mild bloat.
Report points to `/[workflow]:finish` and work-branch jargon, which adds noise for a trivial change.
Change-request handling was good: it named the conflict with D2, retired S4 and updated the README.
Created a `feature/top-n` branch without being asked and without giving a reason.
First version rejected `--top 0` without explaining why; decisions were listed but not justified.
`test_top_zero_prints_nothing_and_succeeds` copies the temp-file helper inline instead of making `run_main` return the exit code.
`test_top_limits_output` and the tie test overlap a little.
It did say clearly that the old 'zero is an error' test was removed and why: good.
Heavy workflow for a trivial option: plan doc, two approval stops (re-approval after a one-line change), two subagents and six suite runs.
The result is split: the code sits on `[workflow]/top-n/work`, while the agreed `feat/top-n` branch has no code, so Saad's requested branch is empty.
`docs/top-n/plan.md` still says 'Status: draft' after approval and completion, so the docs and the state disagree.
Deferred accepting `+3`/`1_0` and a redundant `default=None` instead of a one-line cleanup.
Leaves an open [workflow] topic that it warns will block future work, and verify notes are hidden under `.git/`.
First version rejected `--top 0` with no reason; the choices were not framed as decisions for Saad to check.
The module-level `run_main` uses a bare `assert status == 0`, which is out of step with the `unittest` style of the file.
`test_top_limits_output` and `test_top_cut_within_tie_keeps_alphabetical` overlap.
The CRLF detour (wrong first check, then a revert) added noise to the progress messages, though it ended correctly.
It explained the test changes after the fix clearly, as asked.

summary: K, N and Q did the small change directly, handled the `--top 0` correction cleanly and tested the key edge cases; K stood out for listing each decision with a reason and an alternative. M and P buried a 10-line feature under plans, reviews and branches, and P also left the code off the branch Saad asked for and its plan marked 'draft'.
